section: 22-23: auto placement control points, real GTX 1650 Vulkan

points.label: C_strongly_constrained
points.note: AUTO itself never naturally reached an all-CPU or near-all-CPU plan within gpu_policy's own pre-check window on this host/model (see known_limitations.gpu_policy_not_placement_aware) -- point C is demonstrated via the always-valid explicit 'cpu' mode instead, at the SAME weight placement as points A/B, confirming the mechanism's far end works on real hardware. AUTO's own minimum-GPU behavior at a genuinely constrained budget is covered by the pure planner's test_all_cpu_required unit test (synthetic inputs, deterministic).

point_d_impossible_config.reason: Not constructed as a separate point -- ctx=30000+ at --gpu-layers all on the 1.5B model already fails closed for EVERY placement mode identically (see known_limitations.gpu_policy_not_placement_aware and capacity_uplift.json's rejection boundary), which already demonstrates fail-closed behavior for an impossible configuration without needing a fourth, separately constructed case.

known_limitations.gpu_policy_not_placement_aware: tools/membrane-run/gpu_policy.c's pre-flight check (Section 21-preserved, UNMODIFIED by this phase) always assumes the full KV cache must be GPU-resident when deciding whether a --gpu-layers request can be granted at all, regardless of --kv-placement's value. Verified directly: at ctx=32768 on the 1.5B model, --gpu-layers all is rejected by this pre-check identically whether --kv-placement is unset, cpu, or auto -- even though --kv-placement cpu would need ZERO GPU KV bytes in reality. This means --kv-placement cannot currently unlock a --gpu-layers request that the existing (intentionally untouched) weight-placement guard already refuses. See capacity_uplift.json for what CAN be demonstrated instead: within the requests gpu_policy DOES grant, --kv-placement auto/cpu measurably lets the real context construction succeed where the default (all-GPU KV) path fails at the ggml/Vulkan allocator level.
